parole.testo: Inherited from Late Latin -ittus. Doublet of -ete.

parole.significato: -ment; forms nouns from verbs with the sense of the action or process
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish -miento. Doublet of -mento.

parole.significato: to fall (to move to a lower position due to gravity)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish caer, from Late Latin cadēre, from Classical Latin cadere. Cognate with French choir, Galician caer, Portuguese cair.

parole.significato: title of respect for a woman comparable to Mrs.
parole.testo: Inherited from Late Latin domna, from Latin domina, feminine of Latin dominus ("sir, ruler, owner of a house"). Doublet of dueña and dama.
Borrowed from Late Latin ēlēctōrem (“chooser, selector”), from Latin ēligō (“to choose, pick out”), ex- + legō from Proto-Italic *legō (“to gather, collect”), from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ-.

parole.significato: leaf (usually green and flat organ that is the most prominent feature of most vegetative plants)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish foja, from Late Latin folia, the plural of Classical Latin folium (“leaf”) reinterpreted as a feminine singular noun. Doublet of folio, borrowed from Latin. Cognate with Portuguese folha, Catalan fulla, French feuille, and English foil.
Inherited from Late Latin puncta, feminine of Latin pūnctus, perfect passive participle of pungō, from Proto-Italic *pungō, from Proto-Indo-European *pewǵ-.
Inherited from Old Spanish rio, from Late Latin rīus (“river”), from Classical Latin rīvus (“brook, small stream”).
Inherited from Old Spanish sueldo, from Late Latin soldus, from Latin solidus (“gold coin”). Doublet of sólido.
Inherited from Late Latin trānsversāre, from Classical Latin trānsversus. See atravesar.

parole.significato: to spread, to smear; to rub on (to distribute in a thin layer over)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish untar, from Late Latin unctāre, frequentative of Latin ungere (via its past participle unctus), from earlier unguere, from Proto-Italic *ongʷō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃engʷ- (“anoint”).
